newsitem.title: UK: Ashanti says on track to meet 1997 goals.
newsitem.headline: Ashanti says on track to meet 1997 goals.

text.p: Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields, which earlier reported lower first-quarter earnings, said it was on track to meet 1997 production and cost forecasts.
It added that its Bibiani and Siguiri development projects in Ghana and Guinea respectively were progressing according to plan.
Exploration work at the Geita project in Tanzania and mine development drilling at the operational locations were advancing satisfactorily.
Ashanti earlier said that earnings fell to $15.1 million from 25.2 million as cash operating costs rose $261 per ounce from $212.
Attributable gold production, however, rose to 282,832 ounces from 261,587.
Ashanti, one of the world's biggest gold mining firms, aims to produce 1.1 million ounces at an average cash operating cost of $265 per ounce for the full year.
Total first-quarter operating costs at Ashanti's main Obuasi mine were $272 per ounce, in line with expectations and benefiting from measures taken late last year to reduce costs.
